svg.title: The six Level 1 outcomes, as a checklist
svg.desc: A certificate-style checklist with six empty tick boxes, one for each Level 1 outcome: rules versus learned from examples, building a dataset by hand, training and honestly measuring a classifier, memorising versus generalising, how machines see and read, and fair private honest AI.
svg.text: The six outcomes. Tick them honestly.

g.text: 2. Build a real dataset by hand
3. Train it and measure it honestly
I can sort any system and defend my call,
and say why every AI today is narrow.
Rows, columns, missing and impossible values,
features, labels, leaky features, a data card.
Split before training. Accuracy as a fraction,
a decimal and a percent, next to the baseline.
I have personally built a model that aced its
own photos and flopped on new ones.
An image is a grid of numbers. A chatbot is a
next-word guesser that can be fluent and wrong.
I measured a gap on my own model, in points,
and said it out loud to a real person.

svg.text: "Not yet" is a legal answer here. It is the only one that helps you.
